title: Conormal transport between equivalent canonical symmetric presentations
statement: Let R and A be commutative rings with R-algebra A, and P a presentation of A with n variables and m relations [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let M be any A-module with an A-linear equivalence e from P.toExtension.Cotangent to M. Put I=P.ker, B=R[Fin n]/I and C=Sym_B(I/I²) [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Define phi:R[Fin n][Fin m]→C by reducing coefficients to B and sending y_j to iota(class(P.relation j)). Define f:R[Fin(n+m)]→Sym_A(M) with variables reindexed by finSumFinEquiv, sending the first variables to the coefficient images of P.val and the last to iota(e(class(P.relation j))) [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For every proof that phi is surjective, there exist a ring equivalence rho:R[Fin(n+m)]/ker f ≃ C and a rho-semilinear equivalence (ker f)/(ker f)² ≃ (Extension.ofSurjective phi.toIntAlgHom hphi).Cotangent. R,A,M may lie in different universes; no projectivity or freeness assumption is made.

source.place: The polynomial symmetric presentation preceding equation (16.3.1.1), together with its invariance under the coefficient and conormal identifications; online proof read 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Identify P.Quotient with A by P.quotientEquiv and identify the conormal quotients by the identity on representatives, proved semilinear by quotient induction and Extension.Cotangent.val_smul'. Compose with e. The private exists_symmetricEquiv helper constructs the forward and inverse ring maps by SymmetricAlgebra.lift after transporting the coefficient algebra structures along the ring equivalence and its inverse. SymmetricAlgebra.induction proves that both composites are identities on coefficients and degree-one generators, and respects sums and products. The helper also proves the coefficient and degree-one formulas for the resulting equivalence E.

Define T using MvPolynomial.renameEquiv with finSumFinEquiv.symm followed by Equiv.sumComm, then MvPolynomial.sumAlgEquiv. Its action on constants is C r ↦ C(C r); its action on variables is X(finSumFinEquiv(inl j)) ↦ C(X j) and X(finSumFinEquiv(inr j)) ↦ X j. Prove E.comp phi.comp T = f by MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext. Coefficients use P.quotientEquiv_mk, Generators.algebraMap_apply and the R-A-symmetric algebra scalar tower. Old variables use the same quotient formula and aeval_X; new variables use the degree-one formula for E and the definitional representative formula for the conormal identification.

The private conormal_of_square helper proves x∈ker f iff T(x)∈ker phi using the square and injectivity of E. Use Ideal.mapCotangent over the integers for T and its inverse to descend to the kernel quotients. Check the two maps are inverse on representatives, using Ideal.toCotangent_surjective. Surjectivity of phi and both ring equivalences imply surjectivity of f; define rho as f.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective followed by E.symm, which on a polynomial representative r is phi(T r). Compose the additive conormal equivalence with Extension.cotangentEquivCotangentKer.symm. Check rho-semilinearity by quotient induction on scalars and cotangent representatives, reducing it through Extension.Cotangent.val_smul' to T(r*x)=T(r)*T(x). This constructs exactly the required equivalence and does not use projectivity, nontriviality, or nonempty index sets.

proof_origin.place: The same three-step naturality route, now implemented completely in Lean using symmetric algebra lifts and Ideal.mapCotangent over the integers.

lean.statement:
theorem symmetric_conormal_presentation_transport
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    {n m : ℕ} (P : Algebra.Presentation R A (Fin n) (Fin m))
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (e : P.toExtension.Cotangent ≃ₗ[A] M)
    [Algebra R (SymmetricAlgebra A M)] [IsScalarTower R A (SymmetricAlgebra A M)] :
    let I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) := P.ker
    let C := SymmetricAlgebra (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ I) I.Cotangent
    let φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) →+* C :=
      MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom ((algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ I) C).comp
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))
        (fun j ↦ SymmetricAlgebra.ι (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ I) I.Cotangent
          (I.toCotangent ⟨P.relation j, P.relation_mem_ker j⟩))
    let f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra A M :=
      MvPolynomial.aeval (fun i ↦ Sum.elim
        (fun j ↦ algebraMap A (SymmetricAlgebra A M) (P.val j))
        (fun j ↦ SymmetricAlgebra.ι A M
          (e (Extension.Cotangent.mk ⟨P.relation j, P.relation_mem_ker j⟩)))
        (finSumFinEquiv.symm i))
    ∀ hφ : Function.Surjective φ,
      ∃ ρ : (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) ≃+* C,
        Nonempty ((RingHom.ker f.toRingHom).Cotangent
          ≃ₛₗ[(↑ρ : (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom) →+* C)]
          (Extension.ofSurjective φ.toIntAlgHom hφ).Cotangent)
